jobs.title: Program Manager – Manufacturing Digitalization
jobs.description:
The Program Manager/Digitalization Lead is responsible for enabling, guiding, and accelerating regional manufacturing digitalization efforts while preserving plant ownership of execution. This role supports pilots and early deployments, builds regional capability through expert networks, and ensures successful reuse and scaling of proven digital solutions. The role provides decision-ready insights and structured roadmaps to regional and BU leadership, acting as a critical bridge between plant operations, automation/IT, and enterprise digital strategy.

Regional Program Manager/Digitalization Lead

Position Summary
The Digitalization Lead is responsible for enabling, guiding, and accelerating regional manufacturing digitalization efforts while preserving plant ownership of execution. This role supports pilots and early deployments, builds regional capability through expert networks, and ensures successful reuse and scaling of proven digital solutions. The role provides decision-ready insights and structured roadmaps to regional and BU leadership, acting as a critical bridge between plant operations, automation/IT, and enterprise digital strategy.
Key Roles & Responsibilities

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Standard Duties:

- Support and enable digitalization pilots and early-stage deployments across regional plants without assuming long-term execution ownership.
- Preserve and reinforce plant accountability while providing hands-on technical and application support as needed to ensure successful startup and stabilization.
- Lead and coordinate a regional network of digital and automation subject matter experts to provide aligned, timely support without overloading plant resources.
- Capture successful digital solutions and scale them through standardized playbooks, reusable architectures, and deployment patterns.
- Maintain and communicate a 30/60/90-day rolling regional digitalization execution roadmap, highlighting priorities, dependencies, and risks.
- Provide clear, decision-ready inputs and recommendations to regional leadership for escalation, prioritization, and resource alignment.
- Partner closely with plant leadership, manufacturing engineering, maintenance, IT, and corporate digital teams to translate operational needs into compliant, scalable solutions.
- Enable knowledge sharing and capability building across plants through best-practice exchanges, standards, and lessons learned.
- Execute digitalization enablement activities within priorities and direction established through regional digitalization governance

Other Duties:
This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time.
Additional Information:
Travel is required as needed to support regional plants and pilot deployments (expected up to ~30%).

Safety and Physical Requirements:
- All employees are responsible for knowing, understanding and complying with the safety policies and procedures.
- Wear PPE when appropriate in designated campus areas.

Key Competencies
Digital Enablement and Application Support  Systems Thinking and Integration  Change Management and Influence  Structured Problem Solving  Cross-Functional Collaboration. Decision Framing and Executive Communication
Education & Experience
- Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (Manufacturing, Electrical, Controls, or similar discipline) required
- Advanced degree (MBA, MS Engineering, or similar) preferred
- 7+ years of experience in manufacturing, automation, or industrial digitalization roles
- Demonstrated hands-on experience with manufacturing systems (MES), dashboards, analytics, and data-driven decision support
- Strong working knowledge of automation systems including PLCs, SCADA, sensors, vision systems, and edge devices
- Proven understanding of OT/IT integration, industrial networking, cybersecurity, and IT governance in a manufacturing environment
- Ability to translate shop-floor problems into scalable, compliant digital solutions
- Experience supporting multi-site or regional manufacturing organizations strongly preferred

EEO Statement
“BorgWarner is an equal employment opportunity employer such that all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, age, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, national origin, disability or protected veteran status.”

ACKNOWLEDGMENT STATEMENT
I confirm that I have reviewed, feel adequately informed and understood the responsibilities and requirements of this job description.  I agree to adhere to these job responsibilities and requirements as outlined in this document.

jobs.title: Program Management Intern
jobs.description:
Position
Program Management Intern
Location
Arden, NC

About Us
BorgWarner is a global product leader in delivering innovative and sustainable mobility solutions. We are a company of innovators and independent thinkers that brings together talented employees, meaningful work and amazing technology in a unique environment. At BorgWarner, we constantly work towards our vision of a clean and energy-efficient world.

Our Culture
BorgWarner promotes and nurtures a diverse and inclusive environment, honors integrity, strives for excellence, commits to responsibility for our communities and the environment, and builds on the power of collaboration.  We believe the health and safety of our employees are a top priority.

Career Opportunities
We manage talent as seriously as we manage our businesses and encourage you to learn about our proud history, strong culture, technologies, and vision for the future. We offer positions locally and globally with over 80 locations in 19 countries.

If this position energizes you and you feel you can help us achieve our mission and vision, you are invited to submit an application for consideration.

You may see the list of requirements and feel you do not meet all of them. However, remember that BorgWarner thinks differently. If your qualifications align with the majority of those outlined in this job description, we encourage you to apply and share your experience and skills with us.

For a listing of Asheville/Arden openings: BorgWarner Openings

Job Purpose
The BorgWarner Arden campus offers two world class technical centers and a cutting-edge manufacturing facility that designs and produces turbos, fan, and fan drive components for the automotive industry. The Arden campus offers a multitude of career opportunities and is in the beautiful mountains of Western North Carolina.

Reporting to Program Manager, responsible for organizing, coordinating, and executing a comprehensive project management regimen that meets customer expectations. Reporting to Manager, Program Management, support continuous improvement of existing Program Management processes/tools for Arden, NC.

Key Responsibilities
- Working with Manager, Program Management, evaluates and executes continuous improvement of existing Program Management processes and tools.
- Provides project management for customer programs, focusing on (1) the assertive oversight of product launches, (2) vigilant cost containment, avoidance, and reduction throughout a product’s life cycle, (3) a comprehensive communications effort
- Works at all levels of the organization to build a case for the program and gain the commitment of the department heads allowing the allocation of the necessary resources
- Interacts with customer teams to help develop and lead programs aimed at satisfying customer demands
- Serves as program owner, accountable for the execution and success of the program
- Leads the program team to achieve the financial results the program was approved on
- Develops programs from inception through completion of Quality Gate 6
- Leads customer program teams through established BW PM process. This would include but not be limited to strategic programs involving planning and defining objectives, product design and development, process design and development, product and process validation, and initial production performance
- Drives the APQP process to meet cost, timing, and delivery objectives in a TS16949 environment
- Ensures internal and external required documentation is delivered on time
- Creates and manages program timelines to meet critical milestones
- Manages financial outcomes of the programs
- Maintains program charter, timing plan, and gate review metrics and documentation
- Ensures customer team members are trained on BW PM process when needed
- Establishes and maintains communications with both customer personnel and senior management
- Effectively presents high-level information to senior management and customers
- Ensures that common inquires or complaints from customers and internal personnel are handled in a timely manner
- Develops relationships with customers that make the product launches an experience that contributes to awarding new business in the future
- Recognizes, identifies, and drives changes/improvements to BW PM process.
- Leads program team to meet APQP requirements and deadlines.
- Understands financial reports and engineering documents/data
- Understands and adheres to current quality and control policies
- Understands and adheres to current health, safety, and environmental policies
- Communicates and enforces safe work procedures
- Identifies and closes safety issues (suggestions, inspection, and investigation findings) and their corrective actions.
- Performs other duties as requested, directed, or assigned

What we are looking for
- In progress to Bachelor’s degree in business, engineering, or related discipline
- Experience working in cross/multi-functional teams preferred
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Project) required
- Demonstrated team leadership experience preferred
- Technical competence, problem solving, organization, and communication skills required
- Familiarity with turbochargers and/or engines is preferred
- Solid understanding of engineering and manufacturing functions within the automotive supplier market segment preferred

What we offer
All positions start at an above market pay rate for that position. Benefits are also above market and include the below for all student employees:
- Retirement Savings Plan (401k) with a matching program
- All positions are paid opportunities based on college class standing
- Housing support and travel reimbursement according to policy requirements

Join the company that is creating solutions that support a cleaner, more energy-efficient world. For more information about BorgWarner, please visit www.borgwarner.com

jobs.title: Supplier Risk Program Manager (m/f/d)
jobs.description:
The Supplier Risk Program Manager is a key member of the Global Supplier Risk Management organization and reports to the Director or Senior Manager of Supplier Risk Management. The position is responsible for identifying, assessing, mitigating, and resolving supplier-related risks that could impact business continuity, operational performance, financial stability, customer service, and strategic sourcing decisions.

The role combines proactive and reactive risk management disciplines, capacity assessment, crisis management, insolvency prevention, force majeure response, operational recovery, contract risk mitigation, and supply chain resiliency initiatives. The Supplier Risk Program Manager serves as the central point of coordination between suppliers, purchasing, engineering, manufacturing, quality, finance, legal, and executive leadership teams.

The successful candidate will drive enterprise-wide risk mitigation strategies, support supplier continuity programs, lead crisis response activities, and continuously improve risk management processes, tools, and governance models.

#LI-Hybrid

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Risk Management
- Develop and implement global supplier risk management strategies.

- Establish and maintain supplier risk assessment frameworks covering operational, financial, capacity, geopolitical, environmental, and sustainability risks.

- Support sourcing decisions through comprehensive supplier risk evaluations.

- Create risk visibility and reporting systems for executive leadership.

- Integrate lessons learned from supplier crises into sourcing and commodity strategies.

- Participate in strategic supplier portfolio reviews and risk councils.

Financial Risk Management Background
- Understand supplier financial performance, liquidity, profitability, cash flow, and business outlook.

- Monitor supplier financial ratings and external risk indicators.

- Conduct financial stress tests and scenario analyses.

- Support insolvency prevention and restructuring initiatives.

Capacity and Operational Risk Management
- Evaluate supplier manufacturing capabilities, capacity utilization, and expansion plans.

- Conduct supplier operational assessments and gap analyses.

- Identify bottlenecks and process inefficiencies impacting supply continuity.

- Support supplier productivity improvement initiatives.

- Assess manufacturing resilience and long-term sustainability.

- Develop mitigation plans for capacity shortages and supply disruptions.

Crisis and Reactive Risk Management
- Lead crisis management activities related to:  - Supplier insolvencies

- - Force majeure events

- - Capacity shortages

- - Quality escapes

- - Natural disasters

- - Geopolitical disruptions

- - Plant shutdowns and wind-downs

- Act as primary point of contact during supplier crises.

- Coordinate cross-functional recovery teams.

- Develop and implement business continuity plans.

- Support supplier recovery, turnaround, and restructuring efforts.

- Ensure continuity of supply during critical disruptions.

Supplier Relationship Management
- Act as Single Point of Contact (SPOC) for high-risk suppliers.

- Facilitate communication between suppliers and internal stakeholders.

- Lead supplier reviews and executive escalation meetings.

- Support supplier audits and risk assessments globally.

- Coordinate corrective action plans and monitor execution.

Governance, Reporting and Compliance
- Prepare risk reports and executive summaries for leadership teams.

- Maintain risk dashboards, KPIs, and early warning systems.

- Develop and manage supplier risk management processes and standards.

- Support internal and external audits.

- Ensure compliance with corporate governance and regulatory requirements.

- Contribute to digitalization and automation initiatives within Risk Management.

Position Accountabilities
- Supplier Risk Assessment and Mitigation

- Financial Risk Evaluation and Reporting

- Capacity and Manufacturing Risk Analysis

- Crisis Management and Business Continuity Planning

- Supplier Insolvency and Restructuring Support

- Executive Risk Reporting

- Supply Chain Resiliency Development

- Cross-functional Risk Governance

- Supplier Performance Recovery Programs

- Continuous Improvement of Risk Management Processes

Qualifications

Education
- Bachelor's Degree in: Supply Chain Management, Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Business Administration, Finance, Economics
- Master's Degree preferred (MBA, Engineering, Finance, Supply Chain Management, or similar)

Experience
- Minimum 8 years of experience in:

- - Supply Chain Management

- - Purchasing / Strategic Sourcing

- - Supplier Quality

- - Manufacturing Operations

- - Supplier Development

- - Risk Management

- - Finance or Financial Analysis

Preferred:
- Automotive industry experience
- Experience with supplier distress, insolvency, or crisis management
- Global supplier management experience
- Strong understanding of manufacturing operations and processes

Technical Skills
- Supplier Risk Management

- Financial Statement Analysis

- Operations and Manufacturing Assessment

- Capacity Planning and Analysis

- Business Continuity Planning

- Supplier Auditing

- Contract Risk Assessment

- APQP and Quality Systems

- Lean Manufacturing Principles

- Root Cause Analysis

- Data Analytics and Reporting

- Risk Modeling and Scenario Analysis

- Fluent English proficiency is mandatory

Preferred:
- IATF 16949 / VDA 6.3 Audit Knowledge

- Power BI or Business Intelligence Platforms

- ERP Systems (SAP, Ivalua, etc.)

Leadership Competencies
- Strategic Thinking

- Decision Quality

- Problem Solving

- Customer Focus

- Drive for Results

- Conflict Management

- Organizational Agility

- Stakeholder Management

- Communication and Influence

- Change Management

- Team Leadership

- Executive Presence

Travel Requirements
- Approximately 30–50% international travel.

- Supplier visits, audits, crisis interventions, and plant support activities globally.

Success Measures
- Reduction of supplier-related disruptions.

- Improved supplier risk visibility and early warning effectiveness.

- Successful management of supplier crises and continuity events.

- Improved supplier financial and operational resilience.

- Timely executive reporting and risk escalation.

- Increased integration of risk management into sourcing decisions.

jobs.title: HR Manager Sr.
jobs.description:
Position Summary
The Senior Manager, Human Resources serves as a strategic member of the Ithaca Leadership Team and leads all aspects of Human Resources for a large, complex manufacturing site. The role drives business performance through workforce strategy, labor relations, talent development, organizational effectiveness, employee experience, and HR operational excellence.
As the primary advisor to site leadership on workforce matters, this leader maintains a productive labor-management relationship while supporting operational transformation, organizational change, and future business needs. The role requires a highly visible leader who can balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution and build trust across all levels of the organization.

Key Responsibilities
Labor Relations and Employee Relations Leadership
- Serve as the lead Human Resources representative for labor relations strategy and union-management interactions.

- Lead contract negotiations and effects bargaining discussions while balancing business objectives, workforce needs, and long-term labor relations goals.

- Advise leaders on progressive discipline, performance management, conflict resolution, and compliance with labor and employment laws.

- Provide guidance on collective bargaining agreement administration, grievance management, contract interpretation, investigations, dispute resolution, arbitration preparation, and negotiations.

- Build constructive relationships with union leadership while effectively representing business interests.

- Partner with site leadership to identify and mitigate workforce and labor risks proactively.

- Ensure fair, timely, and consistent handling of employee relations matters and application of policies and practices.

- Develop labor relations capability within the HR team and site leadership population.

Strategic Business Partnership
- Serve as an active member of the Ithaca Leadership Team and trusted advisor to the Plant Manager and functional leaders.

- Translate business objectives into workforce strategies, organization plans, and HR priorities.

- Partner with operational leaders to improve organizational effectiveness, workforce productivity, and business performance.

- Lead workforce planning aligned with operational changes, technology, talent availability, and long-term business needs.

- Support organization design, restructuring, change management, and transformation initiatives.

- Use HR analytics and workforce insights to inform decisions and drive measurable outcomes.

- Support plant performance objectives through proactive management of attendance, turnover, overtime, absenteeism, and employee engagement initiatives.

- Drive accountability for leadership development, employee performance, and workforce capability building across the plant.

- Support continuous improvement and Lean Manufacturing initiatives through effective change management and workforce engagement.

Talent Management and Leadership Development
- Lead site talent review, succession planning, performance management, and leadership development processes.

- Build sustainable internal pipelines for critical technical, operational, and leadership roles.

- Partner with leaders to identify, develop, engage, and retain high-potential and critical talent.

- Facilitate leadership assessments, development planning, coaching, and career progression discussions.

- Ensure the site maintains credible succession coverage for key positions.

- Support regional talent initiatives and developmental assignments across the U.S. HR network.

Organizational Effectiveness and Change Leadership
- Drive employee listening, engagement, culture, and employee experience initiatives.

- Lead the people dimensions of change to improve business performance and organizational capability.

- Partner with leaders to strengthen team effectiveness, accountability, and leadership behaviors.

- Develop communication and change approaches that foster clarity, transparency, and trust.

- Advance a workplace culture aligned with BorgWarner values and beliefs.

HR Team Leadership
- Lead, coach, and develop the Ithaca HR team.

- Establish clear priorities, roles, operating rhythms, and accountability for HR service delivery.

- Develop labor relations knowledge, negotiation capability, and employee relations expertise within the HR team and site leadership population through coaching, training, and mentorship.

- Build capability in labor relations, employee relations, talent management, analytics, and change leadership.

- Create meaningful development opportunities that strengthen the future HR leadership pipeline.

- Promote continuous improvement, responsiveness, collaboration, and sound judgment.

HR Operations, Compliance, and Governance
- Oversee Employee Health and Safety and systems management and partner with leadership to support safety compliance, injury reduction, and safety culture initiatives.

- Oversee FMLA, ADA, Workers' Compensation, and leave administration programs.

- Oversee payroll administration, timekeeping, and labor reporting.

- Ensure compliance with federal, state, and local employment laws, collective bargaining agreements, company policies, and internal controls.

- Oversee investigations, workforce actions, policy administration, and employee relations cases.

- Review safety, payroll, training, and FMLA reports to identify trends and drive corrective actions.

- Partner with regional HR and centers of expertise to deliver effective programs and services.

- Maintain HR compliance, workforce reporting, and data integrity through HRIS systems and analytics.

- Monitor workforce and HR metrics (attendance, overtime, absenteeism, leave, safety, payroll, and training), identify trends, and implement corrective or improvement actions.

Qualifications
Required
- Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Industrial Relations, or a related field.

- Minimum of 8 years of progressive Human Resources experience, including leadership responsibility.

- Significant employee and labor relations experience in a manufacturing or similarly complex operating environment.

- Demonstrated ability to influence senior leaders and lead organizational change.

- Strong business acumen, strategic thinking, judgment, and problem-solving capability.

- Excellent communication, negotiation, investigation, and relationship-management skills.

- Experience leading, coaching, and developing an HR team.

Preferred
- Master's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Industrial Relations, or a related field.

- Experience in a unionized manufacturing environment, including contract administration and negotiations.

- HR certification such as SHRM-SCP, SPHR, or equivalent.

- Experience supporting restructuring, transformation, or large-scale organizational change.

- Multi-site, regional, or matrixed Human Resources experience.

Key Competencies
Leadership
Business
People and HR
Strategic thinking
Business acumen
Labor relations
Executive presence
Workforce planning
Employee relations
Influence and courage
Organization design
Conflict resolution
Talent development
Data-driven decisions
Coaching and development
Change leadership
Continuous improvement
Trust and relationship building

Measures of Success
- Workforce stability, talent retention, and improved succession readiness for critical roles.

- Constructive labor-management relationships and effective collective bargaining agreement administration.

- Timely, consistent resolution of grievances, investigations, and employee concerns.

- Improved leadership capability, accountability, and organizational effectiveness.

- Positive employee listening and engagement outcomes.

- Effective execution of workforce, organizational change, compliance, and business priorities.

jobs.title: Sales Manager – BESS (Battery Energy Storage Systems)
jobs.description:
Job purpose

In this role, you will be responsible for driving BorgWarner’s commercial growth and market expansion in the Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) business. You will develop and execute strategic business opportunities, build executive-level customer relationships, and lead complex commercial negotiations to maximize revenue and profitability. Working cross-functionally with product, engineering, operations, and finance teams, you will shape business strategy, influence future product direction, and strengthen BorgWarner’s position as a leading energy storage solutions provider. You will make an impact through your strategic leadership, market expertise, customer focus, and ability to translate industry trends into sustainable business growth.

Key responsibilities
- Define and execute the long-term commercial growth strategy for BorgWarner’s Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) business across international markets.
- Identify, evaluate, and develop new market opportunities, strategic partnerships, and business models to accelerate revenue growth and market penetration.
- Build and maintain executive-level relationships with key customers, EPCs, utilities, developers, integrators, and other stakeholders across the energy storage ecosystem.
- Lead complex commercial negotiations, including pricing, contract strategy, risk assessment, and long-term framework agreements.
- Drive the acquisition of strategic key accounts and expand BorgWarner’s market presence in target segments and regions.
- Influence product roadmap and portfolio development by translating customer requirements, market trends, and competitive insights into business opportunities.
- Develop and implement customer growth strategies to maximize revenue, profitability, and customer lifetime value.
- Lead cross-functional teams across Sales, Product Management, Engineering, Operations, and Finance to secure and execute major business opportunities.
- Provide accurate sales forecasting, pipeline management, and long-range business planning to support strategic decision-making.
- Monitor industry trends, regulatory developments, competitive activities, and emerging technologies to ensure BorgWarner remains at the forefront of the energy storage market.
- Represent BorgWarner at executive customer meetings, industry conferences, and trade associations, strengthening the company's market position and brand reputation.
- Serve as a trusted advisor to senior leadership on market dynamics, growth opportunities, and strategic business initiatives.

What we’re looking for
- Bachelors degree in Engineering, Business Administration, Energy Management, or a comparable qualification.
- Minimum 5 years of direct experience in Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), with a strong understanding of energy storage markets, applications, and value chains.
- Extensive experience in strategic business development, sales leadership, key account management, or commercial leadership within the energy, electrification, renewable energy, or power systems sector.
- Strong knowledge of BESS applications, system architecture, grid integration, energy management systems, and utility-scale, C&I, and microgrid solutions.
- Proven track record of developing new business opportunities and driving sustainable revenue growth in international markets.
- Demonstrated success in negotiating complex commercial agreements and managing high-value customer relationships at executive level.
- Strong strategic thinking, analytical capabilities, and business acumen with the ability to translate market insights into actionable growth strategies.
- Excellent stakeholder management and influencing skills, with experience leading cross-functional and global teams.
- Entrepreneurial mindset with the ability to identify and capitalize on emerging market opportunities.
- Able to travel (up to 75%).

jobs.title: Sales Manager, NA Aftermarket
jobs.description:
Senior Account Manager
Non-Automotive and Automotive Aftermarket

Basic Function:
The Senior Account Manager works for the Sales Manager and has commercial responsibility for multiple customers. This may include customers in the following market segments; Powersports, Construction / Agriculture, Aerospace and/or Automotive Aftermarket.

The Senior Account Manager is responsible for the daily maintenance of the Accounts. Works with Engineering and Manufacturing Operations to create and implement strategies for maximizing current business and obtaining new business. The Senior Account Manager takes a leadership role in coordination of new business opportunities and quotations.

Principal Accountabilities:
- Represents the business unit to our customers in a highly professional and ethical manner, promoting product leadership in component and systems technology.
- Foster and maintain strong relationships with key personnel at multiple levels of the designated customer organization.
- Utilize these relationships to: - Identify and define new opportunities.
- Amicably negotiate ongoing business issues to the benefit of the business unit.

- Establish long-range plan for volume and sales revenue at assigned customer.
- Articulates a clear understanding of our market share, competitive position and profitability at each assigned account.
- Understand, track and communicate the business unit’s competitive position at the designated customer.
- Responsible for communicating and supporting major customer initiatives and concerns.
- Leads the major quotes for new program awards.
- Develops (with input from cross-functional teams) and deploys comprehensive customer and pricing strategies that are market driven and improve the profitability and growth of the business unit.

Safety:
This individual promotes high standards of safety and health, which stress the importance of preventing accidents and illnesses. (S)he will adhere to Global Star Safety Program, including safety rules, practices, and training as outlined in the BorgWarner Safety Policy Manual, which includes the use of equipment, protective devices, or clothing that the employer requires. This individual will work in manners that stress the importance of preventing accidents and illnesses, and must take every precaution reasonable in the given circumstance for their own protection and that of coworkers. In addition, he/she is responsible for reporting all injuries and/or possible dangerous situations, incidents, or occurrences to a supervisor. Ensures employees, visitors, and contractors (including subcontractors), at BorgWarner, adhere to Global Star Safety Program, including safety rules, practices and training as outlined in the BorgWarner Safety Policy.

Education / Experience
- Bachelor’s degree in engineering or business required
- 10+ years’ experience in sales or engineering with significant customer contact.
- Product (Friction, OWC, SVC) and Market knowledge experience preferred.

Key Competencies:
- Dealing with Paradox
- Building Effective Teams
- Business Acumen
- Strategic Agility
- Customer Focus
- Organizational Agility
- Perspective
- Interpersonal Savvy
- Informing
- Drive for Results

The above statements are intended to provide a representative description of the duties and responsibilities of this position. These statements do not represent an exhaustive list of all the duties and responsibilities required of this position.

jobs.title: HR Generalist
jobs.description:
Company overview
BorgWarner is a global product leader in propulsion solutions. We focus on developing leading powertrain technologies that improve fuel economy, emissions, and performance. Our facilities are located across the globe to provide local support for our diverse customer base.
BorgWarner is a company of independent problem solvers who share a passion for the latest vehicle technology, enjoy working in a fast-paced, collaborative environment, and desire to play a key role in redefining the transportation landscape.
We engage this dedicated group of employees with significant work, outstanding technologies, elite facilities, and a culture that respects diversity and rewards excellence. It’s an atmosphere that fosters personal growth.
Position summary
The Human Resources Generalist assists the local, Ithaca Human Resources team and supports all employees on the Ithaca Campus. This position performs a variety of duties including, recruitment, benefit support, employee engagement, talent & development, and a positive relationship with the operational leadership teams. Passion for customer service is essential to this role.
Key accountabilities
- Collaborate with employees and managers to address root causes of human resources issues, attempting to resolve employee relations issues with a detailed approach
- Participate in company-wide programs and initiatives including but not limited to salary review, workforce planning, organizational change, onboarding, job analysis, new hire and exit processes, selection, performance, inclusion and diversity, and leadership initiatives
- Maintain the relationship with temporary contract agencies and leads temporary /contract employee on-boarding process
- Lead outreach efforts including community service and recruitment.
- Prepare job descriptions, and engage in recruitment-related activities including reviewing resumes, screening candidates, scheduling interviews, conducting orientations, and coordinating any temporary staffing needs
- Assist or owns the student cooperative placement and internship programs
- Works closely with management in the implementation of corporate and campus policies related to human resources and employee development
- Recommend employee relations practices vital to establish a positive employer-employee relationship and promote a high level of employee morale and motivation
- Help implement innovative ways, corrective actions, and updates to policies and procedures to effect continual improvements in the efficiency of the department and services performed.
- HRIS input and reporting monthly, quarterly, and ad hoc metrics and reports
- Assist with internal training programs and evaluate the efficiency
- Participate in employee activities, sponsored events, and special group projects as required

Education/experience
- Associate’s degree+ preferred
- Experience in a manufacturing environment preferred
- Human Resources Experience – recruitment is a plus
- Experience with UKG Dimensions, Workday a plus
- Microsoft Office Suite Proficient, advanced Excel preferred

Visa language (if this applies please leave)
BorgWarner does provide sponsorship for employment visa status based on business needs. However, for this position, please only apply if you DO NOT need sponsorship to work in the United States now or in the future. We are unable to consider candidates who require sponsorship.

Safety
This position will enforce to Global Star Safety Program, including safety rules, practices and training as outlined in the BorgWarner Safety Policy, which includes the use of equipment, protective devices, or clothing that the employer requires. This individual will work in manners that stress the importance of preventing accidents and illnesses. The professional must take every precaution reasonable in the given circumstance for the protection of themselves and coworkers. In addition, the individual is trusted with reporting all injuries and/or possible dangerous situations, incidents, or occurrences to the immediate supervisor.
Equal employer opportunity statement
BorgWarner is an equal employment opportunity employer such that all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, age, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, national origin, disability or protected veteran status.

jobs.title: Sr. Human Resources Business Partner
jobs.description:
The Senior Human Resources Business Partner (Sr. HRBP) serves as a strategic and hands-on HR partner to manufacturing operations and assigned employee groups. This position provides HR leadership and support across employee relations, staffing and recruitment, performance management, compensation and benefits, workers’ compensation, payroll, policy administration, employee engagement, and organizational development.

The Sr. HRBP demonstrates mid- to advanced-career-level knowledge of HR principles, practices, and procedures and applies that knowledge to effectively support business objectives. The position partners closely with leaders, employees, Safety, Operations, and other cross-functional teams to address workforce needs, resolve employee concerns, improve retention, strengthen engagement, and promote a positive and productive work environment.

Position Summary
To perform this job successfully, an individual must have the ability to be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required.  Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

About us
BorgWarner is a global product leader in delivering innovative and sustainable mobility solutions for the vehicle market. We are a company of innovators and independent thinkers that brings together talented employees, meaningful work, and amazing technology in a unique environment. At BorgWarner we constantly work towards our vision of a clean and energy-efficient world.

What we believe
- Inclusion -We value diversity in people, ideas, and experiences.
- Integrity - We believe in transparency, authenticity, and depend on each other to deliver what we promise.
-   Excellence - We contribute to our developments by seeking knowledge and sharing information.
-   Responsibility - We care about our local communities and the global environment.
- Collaboration - We are one BorgWarner.

Key Roles & Responsibilities
Standard Duties
- Demonstrates advanced-level knowledge of principles, practices and procedures in areas such as recruitment, employee and/or labor relations, workers compensation, payroll, compensation and benefits, and managing business partnerships with cross-functional groups.
- Partner with Safety on incident investigation from initial claim to a resolution.
- Strong focus on staffing and recruitment for area responsibility.
- Strong focus on applying and operating within the BorgWarner Beliefs.
- Facilitates a collaborative environment and implements appropriate change management initiatives.
- Provides excellent customer service to support the business through the consistent application of HR policies, recruitment strategies, performance management, data analysis, team progress and taking initiative on challenging assignments.
- Being an enthusiastic team player with a strong drive to create a positive work environment.
- Frequently walks/visits manufacturing floor to touch base with employees for questions, concerns or any other customer service needs.
- Manage high volume workload and not be afraid to "roll up your sleeves".
- Understand business goals and recommend new approaches, policies and procedures for continual improvement in business objectives, productivity and development.
- Provide a true, hands-on approach and successfully monitor the "pulse" of the employees to ensure a high level of employee engagement.
- Flexibility to support a 24/7 work environment that has multiple shifts and a complex work situation.
- Ability to partner with groups to reduce turnover, build employee relations and drive employee engagement.

Additional Information:
- Travel is occasionally required, up to 5% of the time.

Safety and Physical Requirements
- All employees are responsible for knowing, understanding and complying with the safety policies and procedures.
- Wear PPE when appropriate in designated campus areas.

Key Competencies
- Progressive HR experience demonstrating mid- to advanced-career-level knowledge of HR principles, practices, and procedures.

- Demonstrated experience in employee relations, recruitment/staffing, performance management, and HR business partnering.

- Progressive HR experience demonstrating mid- to advanced-career-level knowledge of HR principles, practices, and procedures.

- Working knowledge of workers’ compensation, payroll, compensation, benefits, and applicable employment practices.

- Experience supporting a manufacturing, distribution, or other fast-paced operational environment preferred.

- Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities and a high-volume workload while maintaining accuracy and responsiveness.

- Strong analytical, problem-solving, communication, and interpersonal skills.

- Demonstrated ability to maintain confidentiality and exercise sound judgment in sensitive employee matters.

Education & Experience
- Bachelor's Degree required
- 8+ years of HR Business Partner experience, employee relations, change management, and recruiting
- Intermediate level HRIS, Workday preferred.
- SHRM-CP, PHR certification is encouraged
- Master’s degree is encouraged.

Equal Employment Opportunity
BorgWarner is an equal employment opportunity employer such that all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, age, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, national origin, disability or protected veteran status.
